voice.label: Name
voice.help: What this voice is called. Downloads use it as the file name.

voice.label: Language
voice.help: Which made-up language the voice speaks. Leave it empty for the built-in one. Your game decides what the names mean.

voice.label: Base note
voice.help: How high or low the voice sits overall. Lower numbers sound deeper, like a big creature; higher ones sound smaller and brighter. 60 is middle C on a piano.

voice.label: Pitch
voice.help: Shifts the whole voice up or down. Use it to tell two characters with the same voice apart: +3 sounds a little younger, -5 a little older or bigger.

voice.label: Variation
voice.help: How much each syllable wanders up and down. 0 sounds flat and robotic, around 1 sounds natural, high values sound excited or sing-song.

voice.label: Speed
voice.help: How fast the character talks. Higher is quicker and more nervous, lower is slow and calm. Also sets how fast the text appears.

voice.label: Note length
voice.help: How long each blip rings within its slot. Short values sound clipped and choppy, long values sound smooth and connected.

voice.label: Breath
voice.help: How long the quiet background tone keeps ringing after the character stops talking, in seconds. 0 ends everything at once.

voice.label: Velocity
voice.help: How loud the talking blips are.

voice.label: Motif volume
voice.help: How loud the quiet background melody under the speech is. It follows the sentence: down at a full stop, up at a question. 0 turns it off.

voice.label: Pan
voice.help: Where the voice comes from: -1 is fully left, 0 is the middle, 1 is fully right.

voice.label: Seed
voice.help: Changes the random choices behind the melody. The same text with the same seed always sounds the same; try another number for a different tune.

instrument.label: Wave
instrument.help: The basic tone of the instrument. Each choice has its own character; pick one and listen.

instrument.label: Pulse width
instrument.help: Only for the square wave. 0.5 sounds hollow like a clarinet; values near 0.1 or 0.9 sound thin and nasal, like an old handheld console.

instrument.label: Detune
instrument.help: Adds a second copy of the tone, slightly out of tune. Small values (0.05 to 0.2) make it thicker and warmer; large values sound like two notes at once.

instrument.label: Unison
instrument.help: Plays several copies of the tone at once, like a choir or a string section instead of one singer. 0 or 1 is a single tone.

instrument.label: Spread
instrument.help: How far apart the unison copies are tuned. Small values sound lush, large values sound wobbly and out of tune. Needs Unison above 1.

instrument.label: Layers
instrument.help: Extra notes played together with every blip, like a chord. 12 adds the octave above, -12 the octave below, 7 a fifth. Empty plays one note.

instrument.label: Attack
instrument.help: How quickly a blip fades in, in milliseconds. 0 starts with a click-like snap; larger values swell in softly, like a bowed string.

instrument.label: Decay
instrument.help: How long a blip takes to fall from its loudest point to the Sustain level. Short sounds plucky; long sounds like a ringing bell.

instrument.label: Sustain
instrument.help: How loud a blip stays while it is held. 0 lets it die away after the decay, like a pluck; 1 keeps it at full volume, like an organ.

instrument.label: Release
instrument.help: How long a blip fades out after it ends. Short stops it dead; long lets it ring on and blur into the next one.

instrument.label: Glide from
instrument.help: Each blip starts this many semitones away and slides to its real pitch. Negative values swoop up into the note, positive ones fall into it.

instrument.label: Glide time
instrument.help: How long that slide takes. Short sounds like a quick chirp, long sounds like a lazy wail.

instrument.label: Vibrato rate
instrument.help: How fast the pitch wobbles, in wobbles per second. 5 to 7 sounds like a singer; fast values sound like a trill or a robot. 0 is no wobble.

instrument.label: Vibrato depth
instrument.help: How wide the pitch wobble is. Small values add warmth, large values sound wobbly or drunk. Needs a Vibrato rate above 0.

instrument.label: Vibrato delay
instrument.help: How long a blip holds steady before the wobble starts, like a singer who adds vibrato at the end of a note.

instrument.label: Filter
instrument.help: What the filter takes away from the sound. It only works while the Cutoff is above 0.

instrument.label: Cutoff
instrument.help: Where the filter acts, in Hz. With lowpass, lower values sound darker and more muffled; with highpass, higher values sound thinner. 0 turns the filter off.

instrument.label: Resonance
instrument.help: Adds a whistling peak at the cutoff. Low values are subtle; high values sound squelchy and electronic.

instrument.label: Gain
instrument.help: How loud this instrument is compared with the others.

instrument.label: Reverb
instrument.help: How much echo of a room the instrument gets. 0 is dry and close; higher values sound far away or in a big hall.

instrument.label: Sample
instrument.help: Use a recorded sound file instead of a generated tone: the WAV file's name. Add the file under Sample files on the right (or drop it on the page); your game loads it by this name.

instrument.label: Root
instrument.help: The note the recording sounds at when played unchanged, so the editor can tune it to other notes.

instrument.label: Loop
instrument.help: Repeats part of the recording for as long as the note lasts, so a short sample can hold a long note.

instrument.label: Loop start
instrument.help: Where the repeated part of the recording starts, counted in audio frames.

instrument.label: Loop end
instrument.help: Where the repeated part ends, counted in audio frames. 0 means the end of the file.

percussion.label: Based on
percussion.help: A built-in drum to start from. The settings below change it; anything you leave alone keeps the drum's own value.

percussion.label: Note
percussion.help: How high the drum is tuned. Lower is deeper and boomier, higher is tighter and snappier.

rhythm.label: Tempo
rhythm.help: How fast the beat is, in beats per minute. 60 is calm, 90 is a walk, 140 is energetic.

rhythm.label: Steps per beat
rhythm.help: How finely each beat is divided. Syllables land on these steps, so more steps let the speech flow faster.

rhythm.label: Swing
rhythm.help: Pushes every second step a little later for a bouncy, shuffling feel. 0 is straight, 0.3 swings clearly.

rhythm.label: Count-in
rhythm.help: How many bars of beat play before the character starts talking.

rhythm.label: Rest after , ; :
rhythm.help: How long the character waits after a comma, semicolon or colon before talking on.

rhythm.label: Rest after . ? !
rhythm.help: How long the character waits after a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark before the next sentence.

wave.sine: Soft and pure, like a whistle or a flute.
wave.triangle: Gentle with a little edge, like a soft recorder or an old game console's bass.
wave.square: Hollow and buzzy, the classic retro video game sound.
wave.saw: Bright and brassy, the buzziest of the tones.
wave.noise: A hiss with no pitch, like air or static. Good for s, sh and f sounds.

filter.lowpass: Keeps the low part and cuts the bright top, so it sounds darker and more muffled.
filter.highpass: Keeps the high part and cuts the low end, so it sounds thinner, like through a phone.
filter.bandpass: Keeps only a narrow middle band, so it sounds nasal, like through a tube.

rest.none: No extra wait; talking goes straight on.
rest.step: A short wait, about as long as the punctuation's natural pause.
rest.bar: Waits for the next bar (four beats), a long pause.

division.2: Two steps per beat (eighth notes): slow, even speech.
division.3: Three steps per beat (triplets): a rolling, waltzing feel.
division.4: Four steps per beat (sixteenth notes): the quickest, most detailed flow.

instruments.vowel: Plays the vowels (a, e, i, o, u). Every other instrument copies it unless it has its own sound.
instruments.sonorant: Plays the humming consonants (m, n, l, r).
instruments.fricative: Plays the hissing consonants (s, f, sh, z).
instruments.plosive: Plays the popping consonants (p, t, k, b, d, g).
instruments.motif: Plays the quiet background melody under the speech.

percussion.rim: A dry click on the drum's rim.
